questions.q: What makes IX_Invoices_PatientID a covering index for Billing's query?
options: Every column the query needs — the filter column and every selected column — lives in the index itself
It is the same as the existing clustered index on InvoiceID
It only includes the PatientID column and nothing else
It covers every table in OverlookClinicalDB at once
questions.explain: With PatientID as the key and InvoiceDate/Amount/Status/ProviderID as INCLUDE columns, the query never needs a second trip back to the clustered index.

questions.q: Why run the exact same query from Lesson 5 again, rather than a rewritten version?
options: Changing the query and the index at the same time would make it impossible to tell which change fixed anything
The query from Lesson 5 contained a syntax error that must be fixed first
Rewriting the query would make the new index unnecessary
Azure SQL Database requires rewriting every query after creating an index
questions.explain: Keeping the query identical isolates the index as the only variable, so the before/after comparison is valid.

questions.q: What does the new execution plan show after the index is created?
options: The same Clustered Index Scan as before, unchanged
A Hash Match join that wasn't there before
An Index Seek on IX_Invoices_PatientID, with the Sort operator gone too
An error indicating the index could not be used
questions.explain: The plan now shows an Index Seek directly to the matching PatientID rows, and the Sort disappears because the index already supports the ORDER BY efficiently.

questions.q: Why isn't "it feels faster" considered real proof that the fix worked?
options: Feelings are always a reliable measurement in performance tuning
SSMS automatically rejects any fix that only feels faster
Table size, server load, and caching can make a query feel different for reasons unrelated to the fix
A query can never actually feel faster after adding an index
questions.explain: A structural change in the plan (Scan to Seek) is concrete evidence; a subjective impression of speed is not.

questions.q: What does fixing Billing's invoice query NOT accomplish?
options: It removes the need for any further investigation in this chapter
It does not actually change the execution plan at all
It does not explain or fix Scheduling's appointment-calendar complaint
It breaks the existing clustered index on InvoiceID
questions.explain: The index fix only touches dbo.Invoices; Scheduling's dbo.Appointments complaint is a separate, still-unexplained root cause.
